diagnostic_instrument: No research diagnostic instrument. Eligibility was acceptance by an NHS England early intervention in psychosis service, i.e. 'meeting FEP service criteria'; 40% of referrals (1525 patients) were assessed by the teams as not having first-episode psychosis and excluded
diagnosis_confirmed: EIP team clinical assessment against NICE-concordant service criteria, recorded in routine NHS data; no independent verification is reported
overlap_notes: 20 EIP teams at five NHS sites (nine trusts) in England, approximately 10% of new FEP patients in England in the period. Consecutive referrals mid-May 2019 to mid-July 2020.
employment_selection_verbatim: Patient inclusion criteria were: consecutive referrals between mid-May 2019 and mid-July 2020; aged 14-35 years; and meeting FEP service criteria. No consent was required for the main trial, which used de-identified, routine data. All patients were therefore included. | Service inclusion criteria were: stand-alone service with at least two discrete teams; accepting at least 35-40 new FEP cases annually; collecting NHS England-mandated routine outcomes; geographic and population variation. | No employment, vocational or work-motivation criterion appears in either list, and because no patient consent was required for the main trial there was no self-selection at entry either. The socio-occupational analysis is restricted to the 232 who consented to the societal cost-effectiveness interview, which is a consent-based analytic restriction and not an employment-related one (D12.3c).
employment_selection_source: Method, Cluster and participant eligibility, p. 145

cohort_name: unnamed: Danish national registers, 1955-1991 birth cohort with schizophrenia first diagnosed between ages 15 and 25
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 F20; ICD-8 295.x9 excluding 295.79 (schizoaffective disorder), recorded in the Danish Psychiatric Central Research Register on a psychiatric admission, outpatient contact or psychiatric emergency visit
diagnosis_confirmed: Register diagnosis only; the authors cite Uggerby 2013 for good validity of the schizophrenia diagnosis in this register and note that a small percentage are mistakenly registered
overlap_notes: recruitment_start and recruitment_end are deliberately BLANK: there is no recruitment window in the survey sense. The population is a birth cohort (1 January 1955 to 31 December 1991) alive at its 25th birthday; schizophrenia had to be first diagnosed between ages 15 and 25, and outcomes were measured annually from 1980 to 2016 at ages 25 to 61. Recording the birth years in a recruitment field would let them be read as a recruitment era moderator.
employment_selection_verbatim: Our study population included all individuals born in Denmark between January 1, 1955 and December 31, 1991, who were alive at their 25th birthday. | Individuals were defined as having schizophrenia (ICD-10 code F20; ICD-8 codes 295.x9 [excluding 295.79 (schizoaffective disorder)]) if they had been admitted to a psychiatric hospital, had received outpatient psychiatric care, or had visited psychiatric emergency unit. | Whole-population register linkage with no consent, no recruitment and no analytic restriction on employment. The design cannot condition on employment, and employment is the outcome rather than an eligibility criterion.
employment_selection_source: Materials and methods, Study population and Schizophrenia assessment, p. 1344

cohort_name: unnamed: all individuals first hospitalised for schizophrenia (ICD-10 F20) in Finland, 1988-2015
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 F20 as the primary diagnosis of the first hospitalisation recorded in the Finnish Hospital Discharge Register
diagnosis_confirmed: Register diagnosis only; the authors cite Makikyro 1998 for good validity of the register schizophrenia diagnosis and note that diagnoses are usually made over a hospitalisation of several weeks by several psychiatrists
overlap_notes: One of three case groups separately ascertained in this report; the others are other nonaffective psychosis (fi_registers_nonaff) and bipolar disorder (not extracted). The groups cannot share participants: 'Only data from the first such hospitalization and primary diagnoses were used, and thus an individual was categorized only into one diagnostic group'. Individuals diagnosed before age 15 or after age 60 were excluded. Matched 1:5 to controls without a severe mental disorder; the control group is not a review population and is not extracted.
employment_selection_verbatim: Case groups were defined by identifying all individuals who had been hospitalized for schizophrenia (ICD-10, F20), other nonaffective psychosis (ICD-10, F22-29), or bipolar disorder (ICD-10, F30-31) between 1988 and 2015 in Finland. Individuals who were diagnosed as having schizophrenia, other nonaffective psychosis, or bipolar disorder before age 15 or after age 60 were excluded. | The only entry criteria are diagnosis, calendar period and age at diagnosis. Employment is the outcome and cannot enter eligibility in a whole-population hospital-discharge linkage. The one analytic restriction, 'If an individual did not have data for a certain year, the corresponding case or control participant was not included in the statistical analyses', is register coverage rather than employment selection.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Participants in the Case and Control Groups, p. 251; analytic restriction at Methods, Statistical Analyses, p. 251

cohort_name: unnamed: all individuals first hospitalised for other nonaffective psychosis (ICD-10 F22-F29) in Finland, 1988-2015
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 F22-F29 as the primary diagnosis of the first hospitalisation recorded in the Finnish Hospital Discharge Register
diagnosis_confirmed: Register diagnosis only. The authors state plainly that 'the diagnostic validity of other nonaffective psychoses and type II bipolar disorder has not been evaluated'
overlap_notes: Second of three separately ascertained case groups in this report. Mutually exclusive with fi_registers_scz by construction. F22-F29 covers persistent delusional disorder, acute and transient psychotic disorders, induced delusional disorder, schizoaffective disorders and unspecified nonorganic psychosis, all qualifying psychoses.
employment_selection_verbatim: Case groups were defined by identifying all individuals who had been hospitalized for schizophrenia (ICD-10, F20), other nonaffective psychosis (ICD-10, F22-29), or bipolar disorder (ICD-10, F30-31) between 1988 and 2015 in Finland. Individuals who were diagnosed as having schizophrenia, other nonaffective psychosis, or bipolar disorder before age 15 or after age 60 were excluded. | No employment-related criterion; see fi_registers_scz.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Participants in the Case and Control Groups, p. 251

cohort_name: Jockey Club Early Psychosis (JCEP) project adult-onset first-episode psychosis trial cohort, Hong Kong
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV psychosis-spectrum disorders. Table 2 gives the baseline distribution: schizophrenia 125, brief psychosis 40, delusional disorder 41, psychosis not otherwise specified 19, schizophreniform psychosis 4, bipolar with psychotic symptoms 3, schizoaffective disorder 2, summing exactly to the 234 with income data
diagnosis_confirmed: Clinical diagnosis specified according to DSM-IV at entry to the JCEP project; substance-induced psychosis, organic brain conditions and intellectual disability excluded
overlap_notes: 360 consecutively recruited June 2009 to August 2011 into a 4-year RCT with three allocations of 120 each (2 years EI then 2 years standard care; 4 years EI; 4 years standard care). This report analyses only the 240 who received early intervention. Distinct from hk_easy_2001 (batch F01): different service, different years, non-overlapping age range.
employment_selection_verbatim: The inclusion criteria were: (1) Cantonese-speaking Chinese adults, (2) aged 26-55, (3) diagnosed with various psychosis-spectrum disorders (specified according to DSM-IV), (4) diagnosed with FEP with no more than 12 months of prior antipsychotic treatment following onset. The exclusion criteria were: (1) organic brain conditions, (2) intellectual disability, (3) substance-induced psychosis, or (4) risk of suicidal or violent behavior. | No employment, work-readiness or vocational criterion appears in either list. Employment status was recorded at baseline as a demographic variable, not used to select. The exclusion of the 120 standard-care participants from the analysis is a post-randomisation selection on treatment received, which is recorded on the arm row; it is not an employment-related restriction.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Study design and participants, p. 284

cohort_name: unnamed: IPS randomised controlled trial, Vivantes Klinikum am Urban outpatient psychiatric service (FRITZ am Urban and soulspace), Berlin (DRKS00018107)
diagnostic_instrument: Clinical diagnosis of schizophrenia-spectrum disorders using DSM-V criteria (schizophreniform disorder, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, major depressive disorder with psychotic features, bipolar disorder with psychotic features, psychosis NOS), with the diagnosis validated by the treating psychiatrist against ICD-10 criteria. Table 1 main diagnosis: F2x 63.8%, F1x.5 24.5%, F3x 11.7%
diagnosis_confirmed: Validated by the treating psychiatrist based on ICD-10 criteria; no structured research interview
overlap_notes: perc_qualifying_diagnosis is recorded conservatively as the printed F2x percentage (63.8%). Adding F3x (mood disorder with psychotic features, 11.7%) gives 75.5%. The remaining 24.5% carry a main diagnosis of F1x.5, a substance-induced psychotic disorder, which the stated inclusion list does not name and which sits awkwardly beside the exclusion of 'primary substance abuse disorder'. The diagnosis gate is passed on the F2x figure alone. NOTE the Table 1 arithmetic error recorded in inconsistencies.md: the total-sample F2x count is printed as 50 but the arm counts are 28 + 32 = 60, and 63.8% of 94 is 60.
employment_selection_verbatim: 2.2 Participants: Young adults with EP who expressed interest in EET, independent of their education or vocational status. | Inclusion criterion (iii): express an interest in competitive employment or professional education. | Figure 1 (CONSORT) also records among the 369 assessed as not eligible: 'Other, e.g. are already enrolled in a vocational training prior to study entry (n = 50, 10%)'. | Two D9 triggers are present. The primary one is work intention or readiness: an expressed interest in competitive employment or professional education was a hard inclusion criterion for every participant. The criterion is disjunctive, so a participant could enter on an educational goal alone, which is why the manifest called the selection partial; it is nonetheless an employment-or-education goal requirement applied to the whole recruited sample, and D9 lists 'wanting or readiness to work, an employment goal' explicitly. The second trigger is current placement: participants already enrolled in vocational training before study entry were among those found ineligible, which sits in direct tension with the Participants section's claim that interest was required 'independent of their education or vocational status'.
employment_selection_source: Section 2.2 Participants and 2.3 Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria, p. 2; Figure 1 CONSORT study flowchart, p. 6

cohort_name: unnamed: community-identified psychotic-disorder cohort, university hospital catchment area, northern Bangkok Metropolitan Region, 2017-2019
diagnostic_instrument: Mixed. 277 of 551 were identified from the medical records of patients treated for psychotic disorders (ICD-10 F20-F29) at the coordinating university hospital and its affiliated primary care unit. The remaining 274 were identified in the community: 253 by key informants using a psychosis screening questionnaire (Mongkol et al. 2000) through a modified chain-referral method, and 21 from a 2015-2016 catchment-area survey report of lifetime psychotic symptoms. The WMH-CIDI was administered at baseline 'to assess history of psychotic symptoms and service utilization', that is symptoms rather than a diagnosis
diagnosis_confirmed: Only for the 277 recruited from medical records, where the diagnosis is a treated ICD-10 F20-F29 code. No diagnostic criterion is stated for the community-identified half
overlap_notes: perc_qualifying_diagnosis = 50.5 is 277 of 549 and sits within a percentage point of the SAP section 7 threshold, so the diagnosis gate turns on how the community-screened half is treated. This is flagged in unresolved_queries.md. region = asia_east is a forced choice: the vocabulary has no Southeast Asia value and Thailand is in neither the enumerated asia_east list nor the enumerated asia_south list; asia_east was chosen to match the World Bank 'East Asia and Pacific' grouping, since country_income_level already uses World Bank classifications. Baseline interviews July to September 2017; the first participant entered the programme in October 2017 and the last in June 2018; the programme ended May 2019, lasting about a year for each participant.
employment_selection_verbatim: A prospective cohort study was conducted on patients aged 18 and above residing in a hospital catchment area. | As a substantial number of psychotic patients have no previous or current contact with psychiatric services, it is therefore essential to identify and include such groups of patients in the study to maximize the inclusiveness and representativeness of the psychotic patient population. | Selection criteria tended to be based on patients' symptoms and treatment compliance. Specifically, those with current severe symptoms, poor adherence to medication, problem behaviors (such as substance use or harmful behavior), and no or little support from family members were more likely to be selected for the programme. | Entry to the cohort carries no employment-related criterion, and the recruitment strategy is explicitly designed to widen rather than narrow the sampled population. Selection into the LICM programme itself was on symptoms, adherence, problem behaviours and family support, none of which is employment-related; baseline paid employment enters only as a covariate in the propensity model, which is analytic adjustment and not restriction of the denominator.
employment_selection_source: Materials and methods, Setting and Recruitment of study participants, pp. 3-4; programme selection at Description of the service programme, p. 3; covariates at Control variables, p. 4
